name: swsd_add_incident_comment

short: Add a comment to a SWSD incident

name: swsd_add_record_comment
description: Add a comment to a SWSD problem, change, or release. Set `is_private: true` to make the comment internal-only (default false = visible to the requester). WRITE — does not retry on transient failure.
short: Add a comment to a SWSD problem, change, or release

name: swsd_assign_incident
description: Assign an SWSD incident to an agent by email. Safer wrapper around swsd_update_incident — narrows the agent decision surface to "who gets this ticket." Use swsd_list_users with available_for_assignment_only=true to find valid assignees first. WRITE — does not retry on transient failure.
short: Assign an SWSD incident to an agent by email

name: swsd_change_calendar
description: Show a UTC change/release calendar widget and shared-CI/group scheduling conflicts. Fetches up to max_pages per kind (default 3, maximum 10); ONLY page/per_page are sent to SWSD. All date, state, assignee, group and name-search filters are client-side, over scanned rows only. Defaults to today at UTC midnight through 30 days later. Windows use overlap, with an exclusive end; missing, invalid or non-positive planned ends use start + 1 hour. Rows without a valid planned start are excluded and counted as unscheduled. Conflicts cover only returned items, not the whole tenant. At most 200 conflict details are returned; conflict_count counts all pairs and conflicts_truncated flags omitted details. scan reports pages_fetched per kind, rows_scanned, unscheduled and truncated; when truncated is true, unscanned records may contain more matches or conflicts. No server-side search or date ordering is assumed.
short: Show a UTC change/release calendar widget and shared-CI/group scheduling conflicts

name: swsd_create_incident
description: Create a new SWSD incident. Required: `name`. Strongly recommended: `description`, `requester_email`, `priority`, `category_name`. The created incident's ID is returned for follow-up calls (swsd_assign_incident, swsd_add_incident_comment, etc.). WRITE — does not retry on transient failure; the agent should verify with swsd_get_incident before retrying. To set tenant-specific custom field values, pass `custom_fields: [{name, value}]` — call swsd_describe_custom_fields first to discover field names and (for Dropdowns) allowed values. Validated for Text, Dropdown, Number, Checkbox, and Date types.

description: Submit a SWSD catalog request, creating an incident with `is_service_request: true` (auto-set by SWSD on this endpoint) and the supplied form variable values. Use `swsd_list_catalog_items` to find the right `catalog_item_id` and `swsd_get_catalog_item` to inspect its variables before filling. Each `request_variables` entry needs `custom_field_id` (= the catalog item variable's `id`) and `value` (stringified to match the variable's `kind` — for dropdowns, one of the `options` choices). The created incident's id is returned for follow-up calls (swsd_get_incident, swsd_assign_incident, etc.). WRITE — does not retry on transient failure; the agent should verify with swsd_get_incident before retrying. To set tenant-specific custom field values, pass `custom_fields: [{name, value}]` — call swsd_describe_custom_fields first to discover field names and (for Dropdowns) allowed values. Validated for Text, Dropdown, Number, Checkbox, and Date types.

Strongly recommended: `description` (article body — HTML supported), `state` (common values: "Internal", "Published", "Draft" — tenant-specific). Returns the created solution's ID for follow-up calls. WRITE — does not retry on transient failure; verify with swsd_get_solution before retrying. To set tenant-specific custom field values, pass `custom_fields: [{name, value}]` — call swsd_describe_custom_fields first to discover field names and (for Dropdowns) allowed values. Solutions require `name` keying (custom_field_id alone is rejected with HTTP 400). Validated for Text, Dropdown, Number, Checkbox, and Date types.

name: swsd_describe_custom_fields
description: List the SWSD tenant's custom-field schema. Returns id, name, type (e.g. "Text", "Dropdown", "Date"), required, scope, module, allowed `values` for dropdown fields, and help_text. Useful for understanding tenant configuration and documenting integrations. Default returns active fields only — pass `active_only: false` to see retired ones too. Filter by `scope` or `module` to narrow the surface (the tenant may have 100+ fields). v2 NOTE: custom field WRITES are now supported via the `custom_fields` parameter on swsd_create_incident, swsd_update_incident, swsd_create_solution, and swsd_update_solution. Pass `custom_fields: [{name, value}]` (name-keyed for portability). Validated field types: Text, Dropdown, Number, Checkbox, Date. Multi_picklist and User-type writes are not yet supported — set those via the SWSD UI.
short: List the SWSD tenant's custom-field schema

name: swsd_get_catalog_item
description: Get a single SWSD catalog item by id, including its `variables` (the form schema for service requests). Use the variables to know which fields to populate when submitting a service request. Each variable has an `id` (pass through to the create-service-request tool as `custom_field_id`), a `name`, a `kind` (free_text / drop_down_menu / multi_select / date / user / null), and `options` (newline-separated allowed values for dropdowns). The full top-level item is passed through for power users (description, category, etc.).
short: Get a single SWSD catalog item by id, including its `variables` (the form schema for…

name: swsd_get_me
description: Get the SWSD user record for the token's owner — id, email, name, title, role, department, site, group_ids, and assignment status. **Call this first** when the request mentions "me", "my", or "I" (e.g. "my tickets", "tickets in my group", "tickets assigned to me"), then pass the returned id/email to assignee_email or requester_email filters on swsd_list_incidents (or use swsd_list_my_incidents which does this in one call). Without this step, "my X" queries cannot be answered correctly.
short: Get the SWSD user record for the token's owner — id, email, name, title, role,…

Use this to answer "who changed this ticket?" or "what happened since I last looked?". Cheaper than swsd_get_incident with detail_level=long when you only need the audit history. object_type accepts incidents, problems, changes, releases, solutions, hardwares, other_assets.

name: swsd_link_solution_to_incident
description: Attach a knowledge-base solution to an incident. Idempotent — if the solution is already linked, returns success without modifying the record. WRITE — does not retry on transient failure.
short: Attach a knowledge-base solution to an incident

name: swsd_list_incidents
description: List SWSD incidents with structured filters and pagination. Returns compact summaries (id, name, state, priority, assignee_email, requester_email, category, updated_at) — call swsd_get_incident for the full detail of any one row. Filters use SWSD repeated-key array semantics (multiple values within a filter are OR-ed). NOTE: assignee_email and requester_email are applied CLIENT-SIDE because SWSD /incidents.json silently ignores them server-side (verified 2026-05-08 against the live API). Other filters (state, category, dates, sites, departments, assigned_to_group, query) DO narrow server-side and are passed through.
short: Search and browse incidents

name: swsd_list_mobile_devices
description: List SWSD mobile devices. Use for mobile-device inventory lookup. Returns compact summaries; call swsd_get_mobile_device for full detail. Only documented pagination/layout parameters are exposed for this endpoint.

name: swsd_list_my_incidents
description: List incidents assigned to the authenticated user. Internally calls swsd_get_me to discover the user's email, then calls /incidents.json with the OTHER server-side filters applied (state, priority, etc.) and narrows the response client-side by assignee.email — because SWSD's /incidents.json endpoint silently ignores assignee_email / requester_email filters (verified 2026-05-08 against the live API: a fake email returns the entire tenant). The client-side filter is the only correct way to scope to a specific user. For broader queries use swsd_list_incidents with assigned_to_group=<group_id> (group filtering does work server-side).

name: swsd_my_queue

Each row includes a computed SLA risk level for at-a-glance triage. Supports assignee_email override (client-side filter), assigned_to_group (server-side), states/priorities filters, and sort_by options.

name: swsd_remove_group_member
description: DESTRUCTIVE — remove an SWSD group membership by membership_id, not user id. First call without confirmation to preview the supplied membership id; the API has no documented membership GET. Ask the user to confirm, then re-call with confirm:true and confirm_id equal to that membership id. Dry-run mode always previews; disabled mode blocks. Does not retry DELETE requests.
short: Remove someone from a group after preview
example: Preview: remove group member in SWSD

name: swsd_search_solutions
description: Search SWSD knowledge-base solution articles. Pass `query` for free-text search across titles and descriptions; pass `category` to filter to a category name. Returns compact summaries with truncated excerpts (240 chars). Use swsd_get_solution for the full HTML body of any one result. NOTE: search is asynchronously indexed — articles created or updated in the last few minutes (sometimes hours) may not appear yet. To verify a just-created article, use swsd_get_solution with the ID returned by swsd_create_solution.
short: Search SWSD knowledge-base solution articles

name: swsd_sla_risk
description: List open incidents ranked by SLA breach risk. Computes a risk level for each incident based on due_at and sla_violations: "breached" (overdue or has violations), "critical" (due within 4 hours), "warning" (due within at_risk_within_hours), "ok", or "no_due_date". Results are sorted with breached first (most overdue first), then by time-to-breach ascending, no_due_date last. Defaults to excluding Resolved and Closed states. Limitation: incident list rows only normally include due_at. The sla_violations[] array is only present on the long incident layout, so rows are ranked primarily by due_at and violations are counted only when SWSD happens to include them on the row. Use swsd_get_incident with detail_level long for a complete per-incident SLA picture.
short: List open incidents ranked by SLA breach risk
example: Which tickets are about to breach SLA today?

name: swsd_ticket_stats
description: Summarize scanned tickets created OR last updated in [from, to), defaulting to the last seven days. Alternates created and updated incident-list queries, deduplicates IDs, and shares max_pages across both scans. Totals and breakdowns cover only scanned matching rows, not the tenant backlog or a historical state snapshot. Open excludes Resolved/Closed; unassigned means no individual assignee. Breached uses computeSlaRisk on open tickets at scan time, using due_at and any returned sla_violations (list rows may omit violations). Resolution counts and median elapsed hours use valid resolved_at timestamps in the window only; rows without resolved_at are excluded, never approximated with updated_at. The list API may omit resolved_at, so resolution metrics may be incomplete. An older ticket resolved during the window but last updated afterward can also be absent from these date-filtered scans. Median is null if no valid nonnegative created_at-to-resolved_at durations exist. Assignee/category breakdowns return the top ten.
short: Counts for tickets created or updated in a date range

name: swsd_update_incident

To set tenant-specific custom field values, pass `custom_fields: [{name, value}]` — call swsd_describe_custom_fields first to discover field names and (for Dropdowns) allowed values.
